scientific_objectives: Understand high-energy processes in binary star systems containing neutron stars and black holes.
Estimate the magnetic fields of neutron stars.
Study star birth regions and high-energy processes in star systems lying beyond our galaxy.
Detect new briefly bright X-ray sources in the sky.
Perform a limited deep field survey of the Universe in the Ultraviolet region.

scientific_payloads.spectral_bands: Far-UV (130-180 nm), Near-UV (200-300 nm), Visible (320-550 nm)
scientific_payloads.key_feature: Highest angular resolution of 1.5 arcsec, which is 3 times better than NASA's GALEX.
Possesses the largest collecting area compared to any other X-ray detector in the world till date.
Uses X-ray reflecting mirrors and a CCD for precise imaging and spectral studies.
Unique capability of measuring X-ray polarization and acts as an open detector beyond 100 keV.
All-sky monitor designed for detecting and monitoring transient X-ray sources.

data_management.ground_station: Mission Operations Complex (MOX) at ISTRAC, Bengaluru
data_management.processing_and_archive: Indian Space Science Data Centre (ISSDC), Bylalu
data_management.support_cell: AstroSat Support Cell (ASC) at IUCAA, Pune
